Spruce cones hang down from the branches like those of Douglas-fir while true fir cones stand up, but spruce cones do not have Douglas-fir's pitchfork bracts. The scales of most spruce cones are papery thin--yet another difference. And spruce bark is scaly--Douglas-fir and the true firs have smooth or ridged bark. There are approximately 40 different species of spruce in the world, but only 3 are native to the Pacific Northwest--and only 2 of those are common. document_text: Wireless access points receive a signal from a wireless adapter requesting a connection. Wireless adapters can also be set up to act as wireless access points. In order to mitigate problems from too many devices connecting to a single access point, wireless adapters use a Request To Send, or RTS.

document_text: Volcanoes form at divergent plate boundaries, and at convergent plate boundaries between oceanic and continental plates or between two oceanic plates (subduction zones). All types of plate movements cause earthquakes, including transverse movements where two plates slide along each other, and convergent boundaries between two continental plates (these two types generally do not result in volcanism). Divergent boundaries, or rifts, are places where two plates move apart from each other.
